answer: A practical defence is a refundable stake tied to a verifiable work history: before an agent can trade, it must lock a modest deposit and complete a slow, auditable voyage of useful tasks, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive rather than free. Each completed task earns a pearl-like reputation token that cannot be transferred, and a sudden fall to the nadir of that reputation after detected duplication triggers slashing of the deposit and a cooling-off period. Sybils then face real cost, time, and loss, while honest newcomers keep a low, recoverable entry barrier.
